classic_tracks.title: Dancing Queen
classic_tracks.writers: Benny Andersson, Bjorn Ulvaeus and Stig Anderson
classic_tracks.note: Pop vocals over a disco beat. Start with this if you know the chorus but not much about ABBA.

classic_tracks.title: Starman
classic_tracks.note: A good place to start with Bowie's Ziggy Stardust period. Listen for the change as the chorus begins.

classic_tracks.title: I Feel Love
classic_tracks.writers: Donna Summer, Giorgio Moroder and Pete Bellotte
classic_tracks.note: Summer's vocals sit over a repeating synth line. The song is from 1977; this official animated video came later.

classic_tracks.title: Dreams
classic_tracks.note: A steady drumbeat, soft guitar and Stevie Nicks' lead vocal make this a calm place to start.

classic_tracks.title: London Calling
classic_tracks.note: A louder 1979 choice with a fast bass line and an urgent vocal style.

classic_tracks.title: Three Little Birds
classic_tracks.note: A relaxed reggae song with off-beat guitar and backing voices.

classic_tracks.title: September
classic_tracks.writers: Maurice White, Al McKay and Allee Willis
classic_tracks.note: Bright brass, group vocals and a strong funk rhythm section.

home: New to the decade? Start with a style, meet an artist and find something to listen to.

artists.introduction: Start with Waterloo, the song behind ABBA's 1974 Eurovision win. Then try Dancing Queen and read about how it was recorded.
artists.notes: Try comparing the strong chorus in Waterloo with the dance rhythm of Dancing Queen.

artists.introduction: Explore Bowie's music and stage style. His Rock Hall profile is a useful place to start if you are new to his work.
artists.notes: Look at how the performance and clothing support the music. The source below gives more background.

artists.introduction: Try I Feel Love. It entered the UK chart in July 1977 and is a starting point for this disco section.
artists.notes: Listen to the repeating electronic beat and how the voice fits around it.

artists.introduction: Try Dreams for a quieter rock sound from the 1977 album Rumours.
artists.notes: Listen for the repeating beat and the space around the vocal.

artists.introduction: London Calling is a louder 1979 choice with a fast bass line and urgent vocal style.
artists.notes: Listen to the bass and drums before the vocal comes in.

artists.introduction: Three Little Birds is a relaxed reggae choice from the 1977 album Exodus.
artists.notes: Listen for the off-beat guitar and backing voices.

artists.introduction: September adds bright brass and funk rhythms to the selection.
artists.notes: Listen for the brass parts answering the lead vocal.
